react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge decisively on a single biological story: systemic perturbation of tryptophan metabolism. RaMP multi-database ORA (KEGG map00380) ranked Tryptophan metabolism as the overwhelmingly top hit (FDR = 8.59e-19, fold-enrichment = 875.7, 7 of 54 pathway metabolites detected), with the same pathway appearing in WikiPathways (WP:WP465, FDR = 4.02e-15, 6 hits) and the kynurenine/NAD+ branch (WP:WP4210, FDR = 9.41e-11). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed hsa00380 at p = 5.41e-09 with 6 overlapping metabolites, and mummichog m/z-direct activity ranked 'Tryptophan metabolism' as the single significant hit (p = 0.001428, 16 of 17 pathway compounds matched). This four-paradigm consensus — ORA ×2, m/z-direct ×1 — is a robust cross-paradigm signal. The driver metabolites span the full trunk of the pathway: L-tryptophan (C00078, upstream entry point), tryptamine and indoleacetaldehyde (decarboxylation/alddehyde shunt), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid (kynurenine branch leading to NAD+), and the terminal biogenic amines serotonin and melatonin. Notably, the mycotoxin 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (C19586) appeared only in mummichog, consistent with its known bioactivation by cytochrome P450 enzymes and its structural mimicry of tryptophan-derived indole ring systems in the empirical-compound network. Acetylcholine (C01996) and N-formyl-L-glutamic acid (C01045) are peripheral signals, while deoxyribose 1-phosphate (C00672) maps to the pentose phosphate pathway. The treatment condition therefore strongly dysregulates tryptophan metabolism at multiple branch points — upstream substrate influx, the kynurenine-to-NAD+ catabolic arm, and the serotonergic/melatonergic biosynthetic arm — with implications for neuroimmune signaling, NAD+ biosynthesis, and potentially toxin bioactivation.

MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed the same pathway with p = 5.41e-09, matching 6 overlapping metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity corroborated the signal with p = 0.001428, matching 16 of 17 pathway compounds. Driver metabolites in the serotonergic/melatonergic branch include L-tryptophan (C00078), serotonin (C00780), and melatonin (C01598); driver metabolites in the kynurenine/NAD+ branch include 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) and quinolinic acid (C03722). The treatment condition dysregulates tryptophan metabolism across both its serotonergic/melatonergic biosynthetic arm and its kynurenine-to-NAD+ catabolic arm, with implications for neuroimmune signaling, NAD+ biosynthesis, and toxin bioactivation.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-analysis methods converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed system. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top hit (FDR 8.59×10⁻¹⁹, 7 of 54 pathway metabolites detected). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 with p=5.41×10⁻⁹, overlapping six of the same metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity corroborated the signal (p=0.001344) by matching 16 of 17 compounds in the tryptophan metabolism pathway. RaMP additionally flagged two more specific downstream branches: the KEGG:map00380 hit includes the NAD⁺-biosynthetic kynurenine arm (quinolinic acid and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid), and Reactome pathway REACT:R-HSA-209931 (Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis, FDR 2.14×10⁻⁸) reflects serotonergic/melatonergic branch perturbation. L-Tryptophan is the canonical substrate shared across all three branches, and its decarboxylation via tryptophan decarboxylase (EC 4.1.1.28) initiates the biogenic-amine shunt toward tryptamine, serotonin, and melatonin. Deoxyribose 1-phosphate maps to the pentose phosphate pathway (MUMM:pentose_phosphate_pathway, p=0.060), a distinct minor signal. N-Formyl-L-glutamic acid and acetylcholine appear in sub-threshold mummichog hits and do not reach consensus across paradigms.
